name: Balanced score of a builder's cards on file-finding, topic and orientation cases, with the store's size
purpose: A card groups information on one topic from many files, so a card builder is judged by one number: whether its cards serve a mix of cases (finding a file, the files a topic task needed, the neighbourhood of a file) from a store small enough to be topic cards, at a price in money and time a team would pay.
record: Per builder, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.cards_from_files]), one number per arm per stage. The case set mixes three kinds with the weights of evaluation/cards_from_files/mix.py: the file-finding tasks (right when the needed file is among the first three files of the view), topic tasks taken from the git history of the consumer whose subject names no file or identifier (right when half of the files the commit changed are inside the first three cards; a builder learns only from older commits), and the orientation proxy (right when a file of the target's folder is among the first three files). Store size is a term of the number: a store near one card per file, or over the card limit of the store, gives up that share of every case, so a card per file scores nothing and is a baseline, never promoted. The view is the picked cards in rank order, each card's files in the builder's own order. In the details: each kind's raw result and counted cases, the store penalty and cards per file, the topic coverage of the first card and of the first three, their noise and bundling across folders, cards built, the build's id, its model calls, tokens, cost and seconds (charged to the first scored case).
disadvantages: The cases ask about one Python repository, so a builder good at prose folders is not measured; subjects are developer language written for a commit, some files were renamed later, and the corpus is the pinned state while the topic tasks are earlier; the selector is keyword IDF, not production's hybrid, because the vector half needs an authorized embedding run; coverage is the right files in front of the reader, not an answer found; the mix and the store penalty are set by value and a later set of real inputs should calibrate them; the library's balanced score has three terms, so the store term is applied to the accuracy inside the scorer.
